greenhouse noun

also hothouse, glasshouse, cold frame, conservatory

post-classical

Plin. NH 19.64: intrā speculārium mūnīmenta (Lewis & Short)
Col. 11.3.52 (Lewis & Short)
Mart. 8.14 (Lewis & Short)

speculāria, speculāriōrum n. pl.

noun, second declension, plural

panes of transparent stone or glass; a glazed frame for plants

Not a building but the nearest ancient thing: Tiberius’s gardeners grew his cucumbers in beds on wheels, pushed into the sun and in winter drawn back behind panes (Pliny). Morgan–Owens has the heading “greenhouse, hothouse” without a Latin word, and we found none in Traupman. Pliny has the genitive speculārium.

Examples

  • rūrsusque hībernīs diēbus intrā speculārium mūnīmenta revocantibus

    and on winter days drawing them back behind the shelter of the panesPlin. NH 19.64

See also garden, window, cucumber, nursery.

SourcesLewis & Short: specularis

Pliny, Naturalis historia 19.64.
